intro.data: Two steps: from the form, BUILD a record that bundles the name and age; then PROJECT the name back out. Bring the right builder and the right projection from the tray onto the board and wire them so the original name comes back. One builder packs the fields in order; the other swaps them. One projection reads the first field; the other misreads — leave the wrong ones in the tray.
intro.alchemy: Two steps: from the seed, COMBINE a compound bundling salt and sulfur; then DRAW the salt back out. Bring the right combiner and draw from the tray onto the board and wire them so the original salt comes back. One combiner orders the parts, the other swaps them; one draw reads the first part, the other misreads — leave the wrong ones in the tray.
intro.spellcraft: Two steps: from the caster, WEAVE a blend bundling light and heat; then DRAW the light back out. Bring the right weaver and draw from the tray onto the board and wire them so the original light comes back. One weaver orders the parts, the other swaps them; one draw reads the first part, the other misreads — leave the wrong ones in the tray.
intro.abstract: Notation: (a,b) is the pair holding a then b; the pairing ⟨f,g⟩ : X → A×B builds (3,4) from x; the projection π₁ : A×B → A pulls out the first component, sending (3,4) ↦ 3. From the tray bring ⟨f,g⟩ and π₁ and wire X to A so the round trip recovers 3; the swapped pairing ⟨g,f⟩ (which builds (4,3), giving 4) and the mis-projection π₁? (sending (3,4) ↦ 9) fail, so leave them in the tray. π₁ ∘ ⟨f,g⟩ = f.

afterSuccess.data: You built the record in the right order, then projected the first field — and the original name came back. The swapped builder put the age first, so the projection returned the wrong value; the mis-projection failed outright. A product's pairing and projections only fit together when they agree: π₁ ∘ ⟨f,g⟩ = f.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You combined in order, then drew the first part — the original salt came back. The swapped combiner and the mis-draw failed. Pairing and projection only fit when they agree: π₁ ∘ ⟨f,g⟩ = f.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You wove in order, then drew the first part — the original light came back. The swapped weaver and the mis-draw failed. Pairing and projection only fit when they agree: π₁ ∘ ⟨f,g⟩ = f.
afterSuccess.abstract: π₁ ∘ ⟨f,g⟩ = f: the faithful pairing followed by the first projection recovered the A-component. Swapping the pairing or mis-projecting breaks the law.

reveal.summary: The product's universal property ties pairing and projection together: π₁ ∘ ⟨f,g⟩ = f and π₂ ∘ ⟨f,g⟩ = g. Build a pair in order, and each projection reads its component back.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: fst({ a, b }) === a — when you build the tuple in the right order.
